name: Math
desc: Covers ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, and MOD: portable exact arithmetic, ADD/MUL variadic and array forms and empty identities, strict numeric operands, divisor-sign modulus, value/namespace/LOCAL contexts, eager operand evaluation, error trapping, syntax, and fatal failures. Numeric expectations use small integers and exactly representable binary fractions, without depending on host overflow thresholds, accumulation precision, or rounding. Signed zero, underflow, overflow rejection, and nonfinite extensions belong to implementation-specific tests.

tests.name: Exact addition
tests.desc: ADD accepts individual numeric operands or one array-valued operand. No operands and an empty array both return zero. Values are chosen so every partial sum is a small integer or exact binary fraction.

tests.name: Exact subtraction
tests.desc: SUB requires exactly two numbers and preserves operand order. There is no unary negation form, implicit NODE operand, or array-of-operands form.

tests.name: Exact multiplication
tests.desc: MUL accepts individual numeric operands or one array-valued operand. No operands and an empty array both return one. A zero factor does not waive numeric validation or evaluation of other operands.

tests.name: Exact division
tests.desc: DIV requires two numbers and rejects zero divisors. Division is mathematical rather than rounded integer division: integer operands may produce fractional results. All examples have exact binary results, independent of floating-point roundoff policy.

Modulus and signs
tests.desc: MOD returns a result in [0, divisor) for positive divisors and (divisor, 0] for negative divisors. Sign combinations distinguish it from a native remainder operator. All examples have exact integer or binary-fraction results.

tests.name: Operand forms and contexts
tests.desc: All operands are evaluated in value context using the same caller NODE. ADD/MUL recognize an array only when it is the sole evaluated operand; its entries are numeric data and are not executed as expressions. Other operators require two explicit operands. Namespace references, common expressions, construction, and LOCAL retain their normal semantics.

Strict numeric types
tests.desc: Strings, booleans, null, objects, dates, and nested arrays are not implicitly coerced to numbers. ADD/MUL array forms validate every element, including after a zero product. Invalid numeric operands produce INVALID_TARGET rather than INVALID_OPERAND.

Evaluation, zero divisors, and failure recovery
tests.desc: Every operand expression needed by an operator is evaluated; arithmetic is not a short-circuiting boolean operation. Missing references and explicit FAIL propagate in value context. Match probes may trap INVALID_TARGET, while syntax, resource, and unsupported-host failures remain fatal.

Syntax and fatal failures
tests.desc: ADD/MUL accept any operand count, including none. SUB/DIV/MOD require exactly two operands and have no one-argument NODE shorthand or array-of-operands overload. Unknown expression syntax and recursive resource failures remain fatal.
